title: How Nintendo Really Makes Money (From Playing Cards to Mario Movies)
description:
Nintendo started in 1889 selling paper playing cards in Kyoto. In the year to March 2026 it sold about ¥2.3 trillion of goods, almost double the year before, thanks to the Switch 2. In this file we open the money machine behind Nintendo: the card shop, the strange years of taxis and instant rice, the toy that saved the company, the console hits and flops, why the console is the bait and the games are the catch, the shift to digital, Mario's billion-dollar movies, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Nintendo financial results explanatory material (fiscal year ended March 2026; second quarter of fiscal year ending March 2027); Nintendo corporate management policy briefing (November 2026); Nintendo IR dedicated video game sales units; Nintendo Annual Report 2025; Wikipedia (History of Nintendo, Fusajiro Yamauchi, Hiroshi Yamauchi, Wii U); Inc.

All figures are rounded. The ~97% games share of FY2026 sales is our own arithmetic from reported segment figures. Console units are sell-in (shipped) figures. Movie box office is the combined total of both Mario films as reported by Nintendo. Forecasts are company guidance. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
